5a62824c68: Build00:25–01:20 Music theory basics and the building blocks of music
ac57415e59: Note names, solfège and numbered notation
9e2f673a44: Mi to Fa and Ti to Do are a half step apart
68df9ce0da: All other neighbouring notes are a whole step apart. The major scale's pattern is "whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half".
07907fad44: Highs and lows in numbered notation
ff9c576806: A dot above a number means an octave up; a dot below means an octave down. This course always writes melodies in numbered notation.
11bf60ddd2: BuildNote values and time signatures
69df04d7b1: Note lengths decide how a melody breathes
279db4fe52: 4/4: a quarter note gets one beat, four beats to a bar. 2/4: a quarter note gets one beat, two beats to a bar. The bottom number says which note gets one beat; the top number says how many beats are in a bar.
fb30050fc5: A dot after a note adds half its length again. A dotted quarter note is 1.5 beats.
4e90e9bddd: Strong and weak beats give a melody its groove
63498fca2b: Designing the groove gives a melody more depth. Put important words on strong beats and filler words on weak ones; move the accent in the same lyric line and the emotion changes at once. The groove design chart in the original materials is practice in reassigning strong and weak across eight beats.
f9ce9b7eb4: Pop music: simplify complicated theory so music belongs to everyone
b35db3e2af: Pop music began with the blues; over a hundred years it blended every kind of style and turned the whole world's music upside down.
6fd90eac1d: While US forces were stationed in Taiwan in the 1950s, Taiwan took in a great deal of American pop culture and later became a centre of Mandarin pop.
049692cc3f: It simplifies the complicated theory and structure of classical music so music is approachable, while keeping set patterns and techniques.
231939e9aa: What songwriting is: following the patterns of pop music to join words and melody and tell a story people can sing. Once you grasp the big principles, anyone can write pop music.

519171236c: How a song opens: intro and verse
ac2594b677: Leads into the verse, announces the song, and sets the mood for singer and listener
744221436d: Often the instrumental hook, with strong melody and rhythm; usually four to eight bars, often a slightly changed chorus or verse melody
d0467d296c: Nothing comes before the intro, and the verse always follows it
d0657ec2e0: Tells the story; the lyrics are busier and the plot calmer, warming the song up
dda8663040: The tune is plainer, low and level; usually two verses that set the key and rhyme, with a slight change at the end of the second
d96dea2ab4: Can lead to the pre-chorus or chorus, and can be reached from the intro or interlude
87c43209e2: The pre-chorus builds the heat; the chorus releases it
ebb536d845: Adds the feelings the verse hasn't finished saying; it's where the plot turns. Its syllable count and metre clearly differ from the verse, and it can change rhyme
aaad43f133: The tune starts to rise, the groove is livelier than the verse, and it can use more chords
1d6e3fc8fd: Sits between verse and chorus and always leads to the chorus; it can be left out when the verse already has enough momentum
bba9449baf: The most heated moment; easy to remember and hum, with clear, crisp rhymes, usually the same rhyme across both choruses
b25f26ed5e: The song's selling point, repeated to build memory; the tune is high with big swings, and the instruments' energy and density peak
70a72ed06c: The first chorus is often followed by an interlude, the second by a bridge, then back to the chorus
a0a731070a: A buffer between two big sections that strengthens the instrumental hook
27e5d2b6f2: Often an instrumental solo of four to eight bars; often changes key for a turn, then returns to the original key
8e90c5feb9: Follows a chorus, and can lead back to the verse or pre-chorus
d2ef29fa1c: A more forceful addition after the chorus: the answer, the letting go, the hardest moment to part; it can be left out when the chorus is already complete
4272d48259: A different flavour from the verse and chorus; the tempo can go to half or double time to make the groove's rise and fall stronger
fa6cec13b2: Follows a chorus or interlude, and always leads back to the chorus
6d96085866: The outro lets the emotion out; the ending leaves an afterglow
27962a2ef2: Lets the emotion out before the song ends, so it doesn't freeze all of a sudden
abf5cfbb99: The voice finishes and the instruments gradually wind down; usually four or eight bars, ideally stopping on the dominant to prepare the ending
56313ebb8d: Follows the second or third chorus, and always leads to the ending
32e596b2ee: All instruments stop together, ending on a rest
5c8716e2d6: All instruments gradually slow down into the tonic chord
016c31f211: The overall volume drops gradually to silence
a71c18e6a9: The instruments keep improvising, then stop together
890728f24a: A designed ending phrase, grand and ceremonial
edfffe7ba3: Every sound stops at once for a special effect
